tagline: A web of coastal lakes behind Ninety Mile Beach, made for boating and fishing.
description: The Gippsland Lakes are a network of coastal lakes, marshes and lagoons covering about 354 km2 in East Gippsland. Ninety Mile Beach, just over 151 km long, separates them from Bass Strait, and the lakes drain to the sea through a short man-made canal at Lakes Entrance. People cruise, hire boats and kayaks, and fish from jetties at Paynesville, Lakes Entrance and Metung. The lakes are a Ramsar-listed wetland, home to about 50 rare Burrunan dolphins.

goodToKnow.title: Summer beach patrols
goodToKnow.detail: Eastern Beach at Lakes Entrance is patrolled between Christmas and Australia Day. Swim between the flags.

goodToKnow.title: Summer crowds
goodToKnow.detail: The lakeside tourist towns swell in summer, so book accommodation ahead for December to February.

bestTimeBlurb: Boating, fishing and swimming peak in {months}, when the towns are busiest and beaches are patrolled.
notes: Best months inferred from summer activity and patrols; the research found no further seasonal source. Tagline and blurb lengths estimated by hand, not run through tagline-fit/blurb-fit.

tagline: A gold-rush town turned spa retreat, set among Australia's mineral springs.
description: Daylesford is about an hour and a half north-west of Melbourne, founded in 1852 as a gold mining town. It is one of Australia's few spa towns, with the highest concentration of natural mineral springs in the country. Bathhouses, food and wine, and artists fill the town, and Hepburn Springs lies 3 km north with its Swiss-Italian heritage. The town centre is small and walkable.
whyVisit: Taste spring water from town taps

goodToKnow.title: Bring a car
goodToKnow.detail: Only one V/Line coach stop serves town and the sights are spread out. A car or bike is needed beyond the centre, and it is steep.

goodToKnow.title: Mineral taps are untreated
goodToKnow.detail: Free mineral spring taps around town are tested often, but the water is essentially untreated. Taste a little before filling a big container.

goodToKnow.title: Book bathhouses ahead
goodToKnow.detail: Spa bathhouses are the main draw and many double as accommodation. Book treatments before you arrive, especially for weekends.

bestTimeBlurb: Mild {months} suit lake walks and garden strolls, and spa visits work all year.
notes: Research marks the seasonal guide as unverified (cool, wet climate, 882 mm rain a year; autumn and spring chosen). Owner to confirm.

tagline: A western Victoria wool town with a Guilfoyle garden and a waterfall nearby.
description: Hamilton is a town in western Victoria on the Henty Highway, and calls itself the Wool Capital of the World. The surrounding shire produces as much as 15% of Australia's wool clip. The Botanic Gardens were designed in 1881 by William Guilfoyle, and Wannon Falls drops 30 m over basalt about 19 km west. Grampians National Park is a short drive away.

goodToKnow.title: Falls flow in winter
goodToKnow.detail: Wannon Falls is best in the winter wet and can shrink to a trickle by the end of summer.

goodToKnow.title: Reach it by road
goodToKnow.detail: Hamilton is on the Henty Highway and served by V/Line coaches. Its airport takes only recreational aircraft.

bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months}, when Wannon Falls is at its fullest after the winter rains.
notes: Months based only on Wannon Falls flow. Name 'Hamilton (Victoria)' collides with Hamilton NZ; owner to confirm the display name.

tagline: Surf breaks and clifftop walks where the Great Ocean Road begins.
description: Torquay is the official start of the Great Ocean Road, 21 km south of Geelong, and a surfing hub where Rip Curl, Quiksilver and Billabong set up shop. It is home to the Australian National Surfing Museum, and Bells Beach hosts the Rip Curl Pro, the world's longest continuously running pro surfing competition, held at Easter since 1962. Anglesea is where the road first meets the ocean, and Aireys Inlet has a 19th-century lighthouse still in operation.
whyVisit: Drive the start of the Great Ocean Road
Spot wild kangaroos beside the fairways

goodToKnow.title: Check surf before Bells
goodToKnow.detail: Bells Beach is a serious surf break, and swell and wind decide whether it works. Winki Pop nearby often works in more varied conditions.

goodToKnow.title: Summer is crowded
goodToKnow.detail: Anglesea and the coast fill with Melbourne holidaymakers around Christmas and New Year. Book well ahead or visit outside that peak.

goodToKnow.title: Train to Geelong, then car
goodToKnow.detail: Trains run from Melbourne's Southern Cross to Geelong every 30-40 minutes. Then hire a car or take a bus to Torquay.

bestTimeBlurb: Beach season runs {months}, with crowds peaking at Christmas and the Rip Curl Pro at Easter.
notes: Research flags best months as unverified. Rip Curl Pro (Easter, recurring) is in the blurb only, no seasonalTags entry since tags need months. The kangaroo reason rests on the Anglesea golf course fact; check a photo exists.

tagline: Victoria's oldest European settlement, with whaling history and seal-filled capes.
description: Portland, on Portland Bay, is the oldest European settlement in Victoria: Edward Henty landed in November 1834 and sowed the state's first wheat crop. It has more than 200 historical buildings from the 1800s and a working waterfront where the fishing fleet lands its catch. The 251 km Great South West Walk starts and ends at the Portland Visitor Information Centre.
whyVisit: Walk forest, gorge and clifftop tracks
See fur seals and whales from clifftops

goodToKnow.title: Whale season
goodToKnow.detail: Southern right whales pass Cape Bridgewater in winter and spring, and often visit Portland Bay in winter.

goodToKnow.title: Day-walk the big track
goodToKnow.detail: The 251 km Great South West Walk has shorter sections, reached from roads near Portland and Nelson.

bestTimeBlurb: Southern right whales pass the capes in {months}, the season for whale watching from the cliffs.
notes: Walking has no seasonal source; months based on whales only. seasonalTags kept in the research's {tag, months} shape.

tagline: An Ovens Valley town known for autumn colour, on the edge of the Victorian Alps.
description: Bright is a town of about 2,600 people at 319 m, at the south-eastern end of the Ovens Valley in north-eastern Victoria. Tourism is its main industry, built around the autumn colours of European trees planted in the area. It is a gateway to alpine scenery near Mount Buffalo National Park, Mount Feathertop and Mount Hotham. The old rail line is now a rail trail to Wangaratta, and many paragliding launch sites lie close by.
whyVisit: See autumn colours along the river
Cycle rail trails and riverside paths

goodToKnow.title: Autumn is busiest
goodToKnow.detail: Autumn colours and the Bright Autumn Festival draw crowds, and many houses are holiday rentals. Book accommodation well ahead.

goodToKnow.title: Allow for the drive
goodToKnow.detail: It is about 3.5 hours from Melbourne by road. Public transport is limited to V/Line buses connecting at Seymour, once daily on weekends.

goodToKnow.title: River water is cold
goodToKnow.detail: Swimming in the Ovens River is popular in spring and summer, but the water is very cold, so test it before going in.

bestTimeBlurb: {months} covers autumn colour and warm summer days for swimming and rail-trail rides.
notes: Research gave seasonal tags as strings; converted to {tag, months}; owner/applier to confirm the shape. Summer family-holiday tag omitted as it duplicates bestMonths.

tagline: Little penguins, fur seals and surf beaches on an island two hours from Melbourne.
description: Phillip Island lies at the mouth of Western Port, about 140 km from Melbourne, and is joined to the mainland by a 640 m bridge from San Remo to Newhaven. About 40,000 little penguins live here, and the Penguin Parade at Summerland Beach has run since the 1920s. Seal Rocks, off the Nobbies, hosts Australia's largest fur seal colony, up to about 16,000. Australia's first Grand Prix was held on the island in 1928.
whyVisit: Watch penguins come ashore at dusk
See fur seals and wild coastline

goodToKnow.title: Penguin times vary
goodToKnow.detail: Penguins arrive about 5:15pm in June to 8:45pm in January. Viewing areas are outdoors, so bring warm, wind-proof layers.

goodToKnow.title: Bring a car
goodToKnow.detail: The island has little public transport, none to the Penguin Parade. The Nobbies are over five hours' walk from Newhaven.

goodToKnow.title: Avoid night driving
goodToKnow.detail: Skip unpaved roads at night, as kangaroos and wallabies jump out. If you must drive, slow right down.

bestTimeBlurb: Summers are mild and fairly dry, so {months} suits penguins, beaches and the coast.
notes: Months based on climate (about 24 C in February vs 13.5 C in July) and busy season; the penguins are there year-round. Wallabies appear in the research's experience list and tips, not in a fact; check photo.

tagline: Cool-climate wine country an hour from Melbourne, with wildlife and a rail trail.
description: The Yarra Valley is a wine region about an hour's drive from Melbourne, with more than 80 wineries known for cool-climate Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and sparkling wine. The first vineyards were planted in the 1830s, making it one of Australia's oldest wine industries. Beyond the cellar doors are a wildlife sanctuary with breeding programmes for endangered species, and TarraWarra Museum of Art, with its views over the vines.
whyVisit: Taste cool-climate wines at cellar doors

goodToKnow.title: Public transport is patchy
goodToKnow.detail: Train to Lilydale, then bus 685 to Yarra Glen, TarraWarra and Healesville. For several cellar doors, book a driver or tour.

goodToKnow.title: Check weekend-only railway
goodToKnow.detail: Yarra Valley Railway at Healesville runs only on weekends and public holidays, and Yarra Glen's market is on Sundays.

goodToKnow.title: Take the train, then cycle
goodToKnow.detail: Catch the train to Lilydale and ride the 40 km rail trail to Warburton for a car-free day in the valley.

bestTimeBlurb: Cool-climate cellar doors are best toured in {months}, in the autumn vintage and spring.
notes: Research marks best months unverified (autumn and spring chosen for wine touring). Rail trail dropped from reasons (a spot name) and kept as a tip.
